macro_cross_check.verdict: fail - gap far exceeds the 15% protein bar, and I am confident the SOURCE figure is the wrong one, not my portions
macro_cross_check.reasoning: The source's own serving-size string fixes the portion at 1 drumstick + 1 thigh, which is about 155 g of edible meat per serving. Dark chicken meat is ~19.5 g protein per 100 g, so that portion cannot exceed ~30 g of chicken protein; 64 g would require roughly 310 g of meat per person, i.e. bone-in pieces weighing about 400 g each. The published fat is impossible the same way: 19.7 g/serving means 79 g total, but 27 g of olive oil plus skinless dark meat supplies only ~53 g. Likely cause, and it is the exact each-weight trap in reverse: USDA's meat-only entries list household rows of '1 drumstick with skin = 130 g' and '1 thigh without skin = 149 g', which are yields from 1 lb ready-to-cook chicken, not per-piece meat weights. Feeding those to a nutrition calculator reproduces 57.6 g protein per serving, right next to the published 64. The source made the each-weight error; our portions match the label.
macro_cross_check.band_check: FAILS THIS RUN'S CALORIE FLOOR AND I WANT THIS READ LOUDLY. Computed 358 cal/serving against a 400-650 band. Carbs pass comfortably at 21.1 g (limit 35). I ran the generous sensitivity too - 115 g drumsticks and 145 g thighs, the top of mainstream retail - and it still only reaches about 394 cal and 40 g protein. The dish is skinless dark meat plus low-calorie vegetables with just 2 tbsp of oil, so there is no plausible each-weight that lifts it into band. The band ruling is not mine to make and I have left state at `mapped` with mapping complete, but do not let the source's 527 cal carry this recipe forward: an unverified acceptance would publish a 358-calorie dinner as a 527-calorie one.
